HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
My Legion Pro 27Q-10 QD-OLED monitor has an issue in the HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) modes, where after 30-40 minutes of use the monitor dims permanently until I turn it off and on again. This is not because of ABL, if I pause a scene and turn it off/on in the same scene, the brightness immediately restores and the difference is obvious.
I tried installing the firmware using the steps provided on the site, but it fails the same as it does for everyone else using this monitor, per complaints on this forum and Reddit, since the provided files are not actual firmware updates but a Dolby Vision extension.
Please, Lenovo, upload the proper updated firmware files for this monitor.
This is on the Legion Pro 27Q-10 True Black 400 QD-OLED.

Re:HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
Thanks for the update!
1. On the monitor OSD, switch from HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) to another HDR mode if available, especially True Black 400, then test for at least 40 to 60 minutes. If the dimming only happens in Peak 1000 modes, that helps isolate the issue to that HDR mode behavior.
2. In Windows, turn HDR off, restart the PC, then turn HDR back on and set the monitor as the only active display during testing. If you use multiple monitors, disconnect the others temporarily to rule out HDR mode negotiation issues.
3. Set the refresh rate to a standard test value such as 144 Hz or 120 Hz at the monitor’s native resolution, then retest HDR. This helps check whether the issue is tied to the current high-bandwidth display setting.
4. If you are using any graphics software features such as Auto HDR, RTX HDR, AMD video enhancements, dynamic contrast, content-adaptive brightness, or color enhancement, disable them and test again. Also leave Windows HDR/SDR balance at the default position during testing.
5. Reset the monitor OSD settings to factory defaults, then enable HDR again and test only one HDR picture mode at a time. Do not enable additional image enhancements while testing.
6. Install Lenovo Artery if you have not already, and check whether the monitor is detected there. If available, confirm the current monitor software or driver package shown by the app and apply any offered monitor-related update from within the app rather than through manual Have Disk installation. You can download the tool
here
.
7. About the file you downloaded: the .inf package is a monitor driver/extension package, not the same as a direct firmware flash utility. If Windows reports that the folder does not contain a compatible driver, perhaps you can try extracting both x64 and x86 folder file to Desktop then try again.
Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

So what I've done is the following:
Set to 120 Hz, disable HDR, restart, then turn on HDR. The Legion is the only monitor connected to the PC. I am not using AutoHDR or RTX HDR. The issue does not occur in TB400 or SDR. Also tried before and after setting the monitor to factory defaults.

I've found another way to restore the brightness. When using any Peak 1000 mode and the dimming occurs, switching to another P1000 mode restores the brightness, ie HDR Movie to HDR Auto. However, the dimming starts again after an hour. It's like resetting a timer. I believe this should be a firmware issue.
Lenovo Artery does not show any pending updates for the monitor for me. About the driver, I extracted the zip and selected the correct file as per the installation instructions on the download page.

Re:HDR dimming issue on the Lenovo Legion Pro, firmware 27Q-10 cannot be updated
Hello everyone!
I bought this monitor in January of this year.
The faulty firmware of this monitor makes it unusable, especially in HDR mode.
I run the monitor in the certified True Black 400 mode, and even here it is aggressively dimmed after 30–60 minutes.
It stays in this state until the input signal is changed, the monitor is turned off/on, or the driver is reset via a key combination. This dimming is normally desired with still images or an unmoving picture to protect the monitor; however, it should be lifted again as soon as motion on the screen is detected, and that does not happen here.
This is clearly due to faulty safety mechanisms within the firmware!
To this day, Lenovo has not managed to provide a firmware update, so the monitor is being returned today.
Hallo zusammen !
Ich habe diesen Monitor im Januar diesen Jahres gekauft.

Ich betreibe den Monitor im zertifizierten True Black 400 Modus, und auch hier wird er nach 30-60 Minuten aggressiv gedimmt.
Dieser bleibt in diesem Zustand bis das Eingangssignal geändert wird, der Monitor aus/eingeschaltet wird, oder man via Tastenkombination den Treiber resettet. Dieses Dimming ist bei Standbildern oder unbewegtem Bild zum Schutz des Monitors normalerweise auch gewünscht, jedoch sollte es sobald Bewegung auf dem Schirm registriert wird wieder aufgehoben werden, und das passiert hier nicht.
Dies ist eindeutig auf fehlerhafte Sicherheitsmechanismen innerhalb der Firmware zurück zu führen !
Lenovo hat es bis heute nicht geschafft ein Update der Firmaware bereit zu stellen, daher geht der Monitor heute zurück.

HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10

My Legion Pro 27Q-10 QD-OLED monitor has an issue in the HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) modes, where after 30-40 minutes of use the monitor dims permanently until I turn it off and on again. I tried installing the firmware using the steps provided on the site, but it fails the same as it does for everyone else using this monitor, per complaints on this forum and Reddit, since the provided files are not actual firmware updates but a Dolby Vision extension.

Please, Lenovo, upload the proper updated firmware files for this monitor.

This is on the Legion Pro 27Q-10 True Black 400 QD-OLED.

Re:HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10

Thanks for the update!

1. On the monitor OSD, switch from HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) to another HDR mode if available, especially True Black 400, then test for at least 40 to 60 minutes. If the dimming only happens in Peak 1000 modes, that helps isolate the issue to that HDR mode behavior.

2. In Windows, turn HDR off, restart the PC, then turn HDR back on and set the monitor as the only active display during testing. If you use multiple monitors, disconnect the others temporarily to rule out HDR mode negotiation issues.

3. Set the refresh rate to a standard test value such as 144 Hz or 120 Hz at the monitor’s native resolution, then retest HDR. This helps check whether the issue is tied to the current high-bandwidth display setting.

4. If you are using any graphics software features such as Auto HDR, RTX HDR, AMD video enhancements, dynamic contrast, content-adaptive brightness, or color enhancement, disable them and test again. Also leave Windows HDR/SDR balance at the default position during testing.

5. Reset the monitor OSD settings to factory defaults, then enable HDR again and test only one HDR picture mode at a time. Do not enable additional image enhancements while testing.

6. Install Lenovo Artery if you have not already, and check whether the monitor is detected there. If available, confirm the current monitor software or driver package shown by the app and apply any offered monitor-related update from within the app rather than through manual Have Disk installation. You can download the tool here.

7. About the file you downloaded: the .inf package is a monitor driver/extension package, not the same as a direct firmware flash utility. If Windows reports that the folder does not contain a compatible driver, perhaps you can try extracting both x64 and x86 folder file to Desktop then try again.

Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

The faulty firmware of this monitor makes it unusable, especially in HDR mode.

1. On the monitor OSD, switch from HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) to another HDR mode if available, especially True Black 400, then test for at least 40 to 60 minutes. If the dimming only happens in Peak 1000 modes, that helps isolate the issue to that HDR mode behavior.

2. In Windows, turn HDR off, restart the PC, then turn HDR back on and set the monitor as the only active display during testing. If you use multiple monitors, disconnect the others temporarily to rule out HDR mode negotiation issues.

3. Set the refresh rate to a standard test value such as 144 Hz or 120 Hz at the monitor’s native resolution, then retest HDR. This helps check whether the issue is tied to the current high-bandwidth display setting.

4. If you are using any graphics software features such as Auto HDR, RTX HDR, AMD video enhancements, dynamic contrast, content-adaptive brightness, or color enhancement, disable them and test again. Also leave Windows HDR/SDR balance at the default position during testing.

5. Reset the monitor OSD settings to factory defaults, then enable HDR again and test only one HDR picture mode at a time. Do not enable additional image enhancements while testing.

6. Install Lenovo Artery if you have not already, and check whether the monitor is detected there. If available, confirm the current monitor software or driver package shown by the app and apply any offered monitor-related update from within the app rather than through manual Have Disk installation. You can download the tool here.

7. About the file you downloaded: the .inf package is a monitor driver/extension package, not the same as a direct firmware flash utility. If Windows reports that the folder does not contain a compatible driver, perhaps you can try extracting both x64 and x86 folder file to Desktop then try again.

Best regards,
Hector_Lenovo

posts.author: Phobsen
posts.message_html:
Hello everyone!

I bought this monitor in January of this year.

The faulty firmware of this monitor makes it unusable, especially in HDR mode.

I run the monitor in the certified True Black 400 mode, and even here it is aggressively dimmed after 30–60 minutes.
It stays in this state until the input signal is changed, the monitor is turned off/on, or the driver is reset via a key combination. This dimming is normally desired with still images or an unmoving picture to protect the monitor; however, it should be lifted again as soon as motion on the screen is detected, and that does not happen here.

This is clearly due to faulty safety mechanisms within the firmware!

To this day, Lenovo has not managed to provide a firmware update, so the monitor is being returned today.

topic_info.subject: HDR Dimming Issue on Lenovo Legion Pro, Can't Update Firmware 27Q-10
topic_info.message:
My Legion Pro 27Q-10 QD-OLED monitor has an issue in the HDR Auto/Movie/Photo (Peak 1000) modes, where after 30-40 minutes of use the monitor dims permanently until I turn it off and on again. This is not because of ABL, if I pause a scene and turn it off/on in the same scene, the brightness immediately restores and the difference is obvious. 

I tried installing the firmware using the steps provided on the site, but it fails the same as it does for everyone else using this monitor, per complaints on this forum and Reddit, since the provided files are not actual firmware updates but a Dolby Vision extension.

Please, Lenovo, upload the proper updated firmware files for this monitor.

This is on the Legion Pro 27Q-10 True Black 400 QD-OLED.
